policy_summary:
Confirmed by FOI: within the West Loch Lomond Camping Management Zone there are NO clearways on Argyll and Bute controlled roads, and NO provisions prohibiting overnight camping in lay-bys on their roads. Three of their off-street car parks sit inside the zone.

So on Argyll and Bute's roads inside the zone, staying overnight in a vehicle is lawful. The national park byelaw exempts vehicles on a road, and the council has added nothing on top.
notes:
An unusual record: the finding is an ABSENCE of restriction, confirmed in writing. That is worth as much to a user as a prohibition, and it is the kind of thing only an FOI produces - no council publishes a list of places it has not restricted.

The FOI dates from 2017, when the byelaws were being introduced. Needs re-checking, particularly with the ten-year review live.
open_questions: Re-confirm for 2026 - the FOI is nine years old and the byelaw review is in progress.
Which three off-street car parks inside the zone are theirs, and what are their rules?
Argyll and Bute is enormous and includes the west coast and the islands. Everything outside the Loch Lomond zone is unresearched.
Are there designated aires? Secondary sources mention some in Argyll and Bute without naming them.

sites.name: Argyll and Bute controlled roads and lay-bys, West Loch Lomond zone
sites.notes: Confirmed by FOI in 2017: no clearways, and nothing prohibiting overnight camping in lay-bys on their roads within the zone. Combined with the byelaw's road exemption, that makes overnight stays lawful here. Nine years old - re-check.

sites.name: Three Argyll and Bute off-street car parks inside the zone
sites.notes: Their existence is confirmed by FOI; their locations and rules are not. Off-street car parks are not covered by the byelaw's road exemption.
